queries.text: Why did a US court find Google's search business a monopoly, and what remedies were ordered?
The legal standard and specific market definition used by the US District Court to determine Google's monopoly power in general web search
The percentage of global or US general web search traffic controlled by Google as cited in the court opinion
The number of exclusive distribution agreements between Google and mobile device manufacturers (e.g., Apple, Samsung) identified by the court
The annual payment amount from Google to Apple for maintaining default search status on iOS devices
The share of Android pre-installation slots occupied by Chrome browser versus competitors like Safari or Firefox
The count of antitrust violations found against Google regarding self-preferencing of its own services in search results
The specific injunctive relief ordered requiring divestiture or sale of the Chrome web browser
The timeline or deadline set by the court for implementing structural remedies such as unbundling products

search_hits.title: The Google search-monopoly remedies (2024-2025)
search_hits.snippet: Judge Amit Mehta ruled Google a search monopolist on 2024-08-05; structural remedies followed on 2025-08-05.
